title: Old drum equipment: no sock cymbal, rods, crash cymbal
summary: Early kits had no sock cymbal; an overhead paddle and thin crash cymbals.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: I was going to ask a little bit more about the old style drum sets. When you started, they didn't use the sock cymbal, I guess, then, did they?
No, no, no. No sock cymbal. The high hat or what are they doing now? No. And they had rope.
They didn't have no rods. They tightened up the drums.

They had no sock cymbal. What kind of cymbals did you use when you started? Well, you understand, we had an overhead paddle, you see. Yeah, on the bass drum. And on your floor, B would hit the cymbal.
Oh, as you stroked the bass drum.
Yeah, and they had a cymbal called a crash cymbal. It was thin. Is that the Chinese?
Crash, they'd call it, yeah. Those are different from now.
